hook: Nguyen holds a Stanford PhD combining AI with bioengineering and spent years on deepfake detection at Facebook AI and Adobe before research internships in Fei-Fei Li's and Leonidas Guibas's labs and at Google DeepMind's co-scientist team. He now leads Radical Numerics, a company he co-founded to build what he describes as general biological intelligence.
name: Eric Nguyen

quote.text: I co-founded Radical Numerics to build general biological intelligence.

reading.body:
Eric Nguyen's career traces a single coherent arc: computer vision methods developed for detecting synthetic media are now being redirected toward biological systems, culminating in a company built to pursue general biological intelligence.

His deepfake detection work at Facebook AI and Adobe required distinguishing real from generated content at scale, a problem that sits at the intersection of machine learning and computer vision, the same fields he now applies to biology. His Stanford PhD fused AI with bioengineering from the start, so the pivot to Radical Numerics is less a departure than a convergence of threads that were always present. The rotation through Fei-Fei Li's and Leonidas Guibas's labs, followed by multiple Google internships including the DeepMind co-scientist team, shows a career built through institutional access to frontier research rather than through a single long-term position.

The data does not describe what Radical Numerics builds in technical terms beyond the phrase "general biological intelligence," and it does not indicate funding, team size, or compute requirements. Whether this work is compute-intensive in the way that large language model training is, or whether it sits closer to data-curation and modeling problems that scale differently, cannot be determined from what is here.
